1.title: Quick-Reference Recap
1.text: Welcome to the quick-reference recap. This is an extra module: the whole course on a few pages, for your last review. By the end you will be able to do four things. Match each component to its job, and each need to its object. Recall the levers for Services, storage and scheduling. Name the C N C F projects and what each one does. And translate old names and key terms at a glance.

1.title: Cluster Components and Their Jobs
1.text: Start with the components. The control plane has five. The kube A P I server is the front door. E T C D keeps the state. The kube scheduler places Pods. The kube controller manager runs the controllers. And the cloud controller manager connects the cluster to a cloud provider. Each node has three. The kube let runs Pods. Kube proxy sets up Service rules. And the container runtime runs containers. Everything talks to the A P I server, and only the A P I server talks to E T C D. Exam tip: everything goes through the A P I server.

1.title: Which Object Do I Use?
1.text: Here is the which object do I use list. A stateless app with rolling updates is a Deployment. A Pod with a stable name and its own storage is a Stateful Set. One Pod on every node is a Daemon Set. A task that runs to completion is a Job, and on a schedule it is a Cron Job. Settings and secret values go in a Config Map and a Secret. A stable address inside the cluster is a Service. H T T P routing from outside is an Ingress, or the Gateway A P I. Persistent storage is a Persistent Volume Claim. And limiting a namespace is a Resource Quota. Exam tip: name the need first, then the object.

1.title: Levers for Services, Storage and Scheduling
1.text: Three sets of levers. For Services: Cluster I P is inside only. Node Port is a port on every node. Load Balancer is an external balancer. External Name is an alias. And headless has no virtual I P. For storage: empty Dir lives with the Pod. A P V is the storage, and a P V C is the request. R W O is per node, and R W O P is per Pod. Retain keeps data, and Delete removes it. For scheduling: selectors and affinity attract, taints repel, tolerations permit, the H P A adds Pods, the V P A resizes them, and the Cluster Autoscaler adds nodes. Exam tip: attract, repel, spread, scale.

1.title: Security Layers and Controls
1.text: Security works in layers. A request is authenticated, then authorized with R B A C, then admitted. Admission is mutating first, then validating, and Pod Security has the levels Privileged, Baseline and Restricted. The workload has a security Context, a Network Policy and a Service Account with only the access it needs. The supply chain is scanned, signed, held in a private registry and verified at admission. The current docs describe the phases develop, distribute, deploy and runtime, and older material says the four Cs. Exam tip: who, what may they do, is the object acceptable, how does it run, and where did it come from.

1.title: Probes, Release Strategies and Signals
1.text: Six quick answers. A liveness probe failure restarts the container. A readiness probe failure removes the Pod from the Service endpoints. A startup probe protects a slow starter from the liveness probe. Recreate stops everything and then starts. Rolling replaces gradually. And blue green switches whole environments. A canary shifts a share of traffic, A B testing chooses users, and a shadow release copies each request. And metrics are numbers over time, logs are messages, and traces follow one request. Exam tip: readiness controls traffic, and liveness controls restarts.

1.title: CNCF Projects and Their Jobs
1.text: Learn each project by its one-line job. In runtime, containerd and C R I O run containers through the C R I, and runc starts them. In networking, Cilium, Calico and Flannel are network plugins, Core D N S is cluster D N S, and Istio and Linkerd are service meshes. In delivery, Argo C D and Flux are Git Ops agents, Helm packages charts, Argo Rollouts does progressive delivery, and Kustomize patches Y A M L. In observability, Prometheus pulls metrics, Open Telemetry generates telemetry, Jaeger traces, and Fluent Bit and Fluentd collect logs. Exam tip: learn each project by its one-line job.

1.title: More Projects and Their Jobs
1.text: More projects, by area. E T C D is the key-value store behind the A P I. Rook orchestrates Ceph for file, block and object storage. K E D A does event-driven autoscaling. For security and policy, Falco detects odd runtime behavior, O P A Gatekeeper and Kyverno enforce policy, Cosign signs images, and Trivy scans them. On the platform side, Crossplane builds control planes for infrastructure, Backstage is a developer portal, and Knative and OpenFaaS are serverless. CloudEvents is a common event format, and Open Cost shows spend. And Metal L B gives Load Balancer Services on bare metal. Exam tip: match the job to the project.

1.title: Old and New Names
1.text: This slide is tagged old wording. It is also tagged moving, because of one fact about a controller. Older material uses names that have changed. Pod Security Policy was removed, and Pod Security admission replaces it. Dockershim was removed, and nodes need a C R I runtime such as containerd or C R I O. The Endpoints A P I is deprecated, and Endpoint Slices replace it. Ingress is frozen, and Gateway A P I is the successor. The four Cs became the lifecycle phases. And the five domains, forty-six, twenty-two, sixteen, eight and eight, became four, forty-four, twenty-eight, sixteen and twelve. As of the thirtieth of October, twenty twenty-six, the Ingress Nginx controller is retired. Exam tip: map an old name to its new home.

1.title: Key Terms in One Line
1.text: Ten terms in one line each. A Pod is the smallest deployable unit, with containers that share network and storage. A namespace divides a cluster, and scopes names and quotas. Labels are key-value tags, and selectors are the queries that connect objects. A C R D is a new A P I kind, and an operator is a controller that manages an application. A taint repels, and a toleration permits. A sidecar is a helper container in the same Pod. Drift is the actual state moving away from the desired state. S L I, S L O and S L A are a measurement, a target and a contract. Immutable infrastructure means replace rather than change. And idempotent means the same result when repeated. Exam tip: if a term is new in a question, find it here first.

1.title: More Key Terms in One Line
1.text: Nine more terms. A controller is a loop that compares the actual state with the desired state, and acts. Reconciliation is the repeated act of moving the actual state toward the desired state. Requests are what a container reserves for placement, and limits are the most it may use. An Ingress controller is the program that applies the rules of Ingress objects. A P V is a piece of storage, and a P V C is the request for it. R B A C uses roles and bindings to decide who may do what in the A P I. An admission controller can change or reject an object before it is stored. Git Ops keeps the desired state in Git, with an agent that keeps the cluster in line. And the error budget is the share of failures that the S L O allows. Exam tip: the glossary file of this module lists many more terms.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: To recap. Components: the A P I server in the middle, E T C D behind it, the scheduler and controllers beside it, and the kube let and proxy on nodes. Objects: match the need to a Deployment, Stateful Set, Daemon Set, Job, Service, Ingress, Persistent Volume Claim or Resource Quota. Levers: Service types, storage modes and scheduling levers, each with a direction. Security and delivery: the request path, Pod Security and the supply chain, then probes and release strategies. And projects and names: one-line jobs, and old names mapped to new ones.
